title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits & Onboarding (Comprehensive Guide)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document is the canonical Redwood employee handbook reference for new and existing employees. It covers how we work at Redwood, our roles and career ladders, the benefits and perks available, the hiring and onboarding process, and practical guides to the internal tools you will use every day.

Who this is for
- New hires (all levels)
- Managers and hiring teams
- People Ops and HR partners
- Engineering and product leads onboarding teammates

1) Working at Redwood — culture and practical expectations

Intro
Redwood is an engineering-first company focused on reliable, cost-effective LLM inference. We value ownership, pragmatic experimentation, and clear communication. Our working norms emphasize asynchronous collaboration, strong documentation, and customer-obsessed product decisions.

Core principles
- Move fast but with care: ship iteratively, validate with data, and protect production reliability.
- Ownership and clarity: individuals own outcomes; teams document APIs, runbooks, and SLOs.
- Collaboration over hierarchy: decisions should be surfaced, documented, and reviewed.
- Continuous learning: internal knowledge sharing, brown-bags, and learning stipends support career growth.

Working patterns and expectations
- Core hours and meetings: teams generally run asynchronous-first workflows with agreed core overlap (defaults: 10:00-15:00 local time).
- Remote-first: we support distributed teams across NA, EU, and APAC. Team-specific cadence and office policies are in each team’s playbook.
- Time off: encourage full use of vacation and recharge time; see Benefits section for details.

2) Roles & career ladders

High-level ladder structure (applies to Engineering/Product/Design/Research)
- IC track: IC1 (entry) → IC2 → IC3 (senior) → IC4 (staff) → IC5 (principal)
- Management track: Mgr1 (first-line) → Mgr2 (senior manager) → Dir → Senior Dir

Role expectations and competencies
Each level is defined by competencies across:
- Impact (scope & measurable outcomes)
- Technical skill or craft mastery
- Leadership & partnership (influence beyond immediate team)
- Execution (reliability, delivery, and operational excellence)

Promotion process (summary)
1. Candidate prepares an updated role packet (impact examples, metrics, feedback).
2. Manager compiles feedback and recommends promotion to People Ops.
3. Panel review: cross-functional reviewers evaluate evidence against the ladder rubric.
4. Decision & calibration: final decision recorded and communicated; compensation and leveling adjustments follow standard cadence.

Typical timelines
- Promotion cycles: biannual formal cycles (June and December) plus rare off-cycle promotions for exceptional cases.
- Probation/initial review: 90-day check-in and 6-month onboarding review for new hires.

Ownership: People Ops maintains ladder rubrics and templates. Managers are responsible for coaching and promotion packet preparation.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision plans (US) with options for single/family coverage; EU/UK benefits vary by location — People Ops will provide local plan specifics at offer time.
- Mental health support: EAP and reimbursement for therapy sessions (country-specific limits apply).

Compensation & equity
- Competitive base pay with role and market benchmarking.
- Annual equity grants for full-time hires; refresh cadence determined by role and tenure.
- Bonus/variable compensation: eligibility and targets are defined in offer letters and compensation docs.

Time off & parental leave
- PTO: flexible paid time off policy with recommended minimum of 20 working days/year; statutory leave applies locally.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver up to 18 weeks (varies by location), secondary caregiver up to 8 weeks; detailed policy in People Ops portal.
- Holidays: company-observed holidays + floating holiday allowance.

Learning & development
- Learning stipend: $1,000/year (pro-rated at hire) for books, courses, and conferences.
- Internal training: monthly brown-bags, onboarding bootcamps, and mentoring programs.

Remote work & home office
- Home office stipend: one-time equipment stipend on hire; annual refresh for remote-first employees.
- Co-working and office access: paid desk reservations and allowances per regional policy.

Perks
- Monthly wellness reimbursement, commuter allowances (region-dependent), and discounts on partner services.
- Team budget for offsites and social events.

How to get benefits support
- For questions about benefits, open a ticket with People Ops via the HR portal or email people-ops@redwood.com.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring process (standard for IC and PM roles)
1. Hiring manager raises requisition and gets approval from Finance + People Ops.
2. Sourcing and screening: Recruiter screens candidates, followed by a short phone screen with hiring manager.
3. Interview loop: For IC roles typically includes technical screen (30-60m), coding/design/architecture interview, and a final behavioral/manager interview.
4. Debrief & decision: interviewers submit feedback using the standard rubric; hiring committee reviews for calibration.
5. Offer & acceptance: offer created by Recruiter + People Ops, includes compensation, equity, and start date.
6. Background check and references: contingent on local law and role seniority.

Interview timelines (typical)
- From first screen to offer: 3-6 weeks for most roles.
- Executive and highly specialized roles may take longer (6-12 weeks).

New hire onboarding checklist (quick summary)
- Pre-first-day: IT & People Ops create accounts (Okta, email, GitHub invite), ship equipment, and schedule initial meetings.
- Day 1: welcome call, company orientation, manager 1:1, setup passes for tools.
- Week 1: complete security training, ACLs for repos and cloud, team onboarding sessions, and first onboarding tasks.
- 30/60/90 plan: manager and new hire agree on clear objectives for the first 90 days; milestones documented in the People Ops onboarding template.

Onboarding owner and escalation
- Primary owner: hiring manager until 90-day check-in.
- People Ops provides centralized onboarding support and reminders.
- Escalation path: hiring manager → People Ops → HR Business Partner.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference & how-to)

Account access and identity
- Okta: single sign-on for most services (Slack, Confluence, GitHub, cloud consoles). Request access via the IT ticket portal if automatic provisioning fails.

Communication
- Slack: primary communication channel. Use team channels for work, #announcements for company-wide notices, and #random for social. Keep PII and customer data out of public channels.

Documentation & knowledge base
- Confluence: canonical docs for teams, runbooks, and policies. Create pages under the appropriate space. Use the page template for runbooks and incident reports.

Code, repos, and review process
- GitHub (organization: redwood-inference): standard branch naming: feature/<ticket-id>-short-name.
- PR process: include a description of changes, testing notes, and link to related runbooks or design docs. Required reviewers: 1+ peer, 1 owner for impacted subsystems.

CI/CD & deployments
- CI: CircleCI/GitHub Actions (team-specific). Merge to main triggers canary deployments to staging; production deploys require two approvers and successful health checks.
- Rollback: see the deployment runbook in /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks.

PagerDuty & oncall
- Oncall rotations, alerts, and escalation policies documented in the eng-sre space. New oncall assignees must complete the oncall bootcamp.

Expenses & payroll
- Expense submission: use Expensify with receipts within 30 days. Payroll and benefits questions to payroll@redwood.com.

IT support & hardware
- Hardware requests & repairs: submit an IT ticket. Stock: standard MacBook Pro 14" or equivalent Linux laptop; first-time home office stipend available on hire.

6) Practical checklists and templates (quick links)

- New hire 30/60/90 template: /confluence/people-ops/new-hire-templates
- Promotion packet template: /confluence/people-ops/promotion-templates
- Security & compliance onboarding: /confluence/security-and-compliance/onboarding-checklist
- Deployment runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/deployment-runbook

7) FAQs (top questions)

Q: Who do I contact for benefits questions?
A: People Ops via HR portal or people-ops@redwood.com.

Q: How often are performance reviews?
A: Formal performance reviews are annual with biannual calibration conversations; informal feedback should be continuous.

Q: Can I work from a different country?
A: Remote work across countries requires People Ops approval and local legal/compensation coordination; talk to your recruiter or People Ops lead.

8) Ownership and maintenance
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
- Review cadence: annual review of handbook content or sooner when policy/legal changes occur.
- Related maintainers: Engineering leadership (for role ladders), Finance (for compensation/equity specifics), Security (for compliance and onboarding).

Appendix: Example onboarding day 1 schedule
- 09:00: Welcome & company orientation (People Ops)
- 10:00: Manager 1:1 (team goals & 30/60/90)
- 11:00: Setup accounts & security training
- 13:00: Lunch with buddy
- 14:00: Team kickoff & first tasks
- 16:00: Check-in and wrap-up

For updates or questions about this document, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.com).
